solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film invalid — delete freely

indicators.note: the letters are to be arranged freely, in any order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A curt editorial note telling someone to cut a worthless film without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'delete freely' look like an instruction to an editor; in fact both words before it are raw letters for the Bond film title.
explanation.definitionFit: A title: the 1973 James Bond film, Roger Moore's first as 007, takes its name from the Paul McCartney theme song.

clue.text: Noble queen left with earl hosted by loquacious heroine

indicators.note: 'with' means accompanied by, so earl travels alongside queen and left into the same host
a host takes guests in, so the talkative word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lady is a noblewoman
chatty = talkative; it hosts the next three pieces
ER = Elizabeth Regina
standard abbreviation
E = earl, as in peerage lists

explanation.surface: A gossipy heroine entertains a titled queen and an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' looks like the definition, but it supplies only the first word; the heroine is the definition, and 'hosted by' makes the talkative word wrap the royal and peerage abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Chatterley is the heroine of D. H. Lawrence's novel Lady Chatterley's Lover.

clue.text: Large fiddle comprises half of offences

indicators.note: half of means only the first five of the ten letters are kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: violations are offences, breaches of a rule or law

explanation.surface: A big con includes half of all criminal charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' tempts as a swindle, but here it is the violin family; 'comprises' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is a stringed instrument slightly bigger than the violin, which is informally called a fiddle.

clue.text: Symbolic storyteller building toy trails around houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the rearranged letters take the toy inside them
around here means moved about, so the letters of trails are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of trails, taken as written
Lego is the plastic building-brick toy

explanation.surface: Someone builds with a child's toy while trailing around houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the anagram signal, but 'building toy' is LEGO; 'around' jumbles trails, and the result 'houses' LEGO.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegorist writes allegories, stories whose characters and events stand for hidden meanings.

clue.text: Tried to get connection put up on type of display?

parts.note: laid = put (down)
LED = light-emitting diode display

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hook up a connection to some kind of screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' is one instruction: LAID written upwards. The question mark flags that LED is only one type of display.
explanation.definitionFit: To dial a number is to try to get a telephone connection.

clue.text: Intensify limit of humanitarian assistance, mainly in European church

indicators.note: in places the gathered letters inside the European and church letters

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

indicators.note: limit of means the furthest point, here the last letter of humanitarian

parts.note: the word humanitarian, whose final letter is taken

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so the last letter of the word for assistance is dropped

parts.note: a hand is help or assistance, as in giving someone a hand

explanation.surface: A call to boost aid efforts reaching a church in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limit' could be either end of humanitarian; only the last letter fits. 'mainly' trims the word for assistance, and 'in' sets both inside European plus church.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to heighten or increase, so intensify is a close synonym.

clue.text: Mysterious closure of blood vessel

indicators.note: the letter that closes the word, its last

parts.note: last letter of blood
Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A strange blockage in a blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood vessel' is one medical phrase, but it splits in two: 'vessel' is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark means hidden or obscure, as in dark secrets.

clue.text: Found 10 packed in box south of river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
crated = packed in a crate

explanation.surface: Something is found packed in a box downstream of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is ABHORRENT, so the definition reads 'found abhorrent'. 'Found' looks like 'discovered', but here it means 'judged'.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate something is to find it abhorrent and denounce it.

clue.text: What might be seen as positive symbol for part of the UK

definitions.meaning: the surface pushes an upbeat emblem; the setter means the plus sign, +, as marked on a battery
England, whose flag is a red upright cross on white, shaped like +

explanation.surface: An upbeat emblem representing one of the home nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positive' seems to mean upbeat, but the positive symbol is +. England's flag has exactly that shape. St Andrew's Cross (Scotland) is an X, not a +.
explanation.definitionFit: St George's Cross is the flag of England, a red plus-shaped cross on white.

clue.text: Amusing pretty girl runs boards

indicators.note: to board is to take someone in as a lodger

parts.note: a doll is dated slang for a pretty girl
R = runs, in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An entertaining pretty girl manages a boarding house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs boards' sounds like managing a lodging house; here 'boards' means takes in as a lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry or odd way.

clue.text: Obscene rating split half of "horsey" bores

indicators.note: bores means drills into, so the half word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
rent is the past tense of rend, so it means split

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of its six letters are kept

parts.note: the word horsey, whose first half is kept

explanation.surface: A crude remark from a rating at odds with some tedious horsey people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bores' looks like a noun for dull people, but it is the insertion signal: HOR (half of horsey) bores into AB + RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means repugnant or loathsome, and obscene is used in the same sense of morally offensive.

clue.text: Finally suing after Guardian feature covers substituted child

indicators.note: after puts the final letter of suing behind the rest
covers means wraps round, so the facial feature encloses the word for guardian

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
a guardian angel watches over someone, so Guardian gives angel

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of suing is used

parts.note: the word suing, whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature covers a lawsuit over a swapped baby.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian reads as the newspaper, but it is the guardian angel; the facial feature 'covers' it, and the last letter from 'Finally suing' goes 'after', giving CHANGELIN plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy child left in place of a human baby stolen away.

clue.text: Lavish with compliments?

definitions.meaning: 'with compliments' is printed on things given at no charge

explanation.surface: Someone is heaping on the praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about flattery, but 'with compliments' is the phrase on a free gift, and being free with money means being lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Free means both generous and complimentary, without charge.

clue.text: Lawmaker on trial — so unexpected

indicators.note: the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
TRIAL SO rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician finds themselves on trial, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word, but it gives LEG: in cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislator is a member of a law-making body.

clue.text: Guaranteed return of some comrade Russians one's abandoned

indicators.note: return of means going back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
abandoned means left behind, so the letter for one is dropped
some means only part of, so the opening and closing letters of comrade Russians are cut away, keeping a run that spans the two words

parts.note: the letters of these two words, from which a middle stretch is kept
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for is, linking to abandoned

explanation.surface: A promise that some Soviet comrades will be sent home, with one left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' finds DERUSSIA inside 'comrade Russians'; 'one's abandoned' drops the I to leave DERUSSA, and 'return of' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured means made certain or secured, the same as guaranteed.

clue.text: Instrument captured spirit

parts.note: snared = caught in a trap
rum is a spirit (drink)

explanation.surface: A tool that trapped a ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a ghost to go with 'captured', but it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched across its underside.

clue.text: Horse trainers encourage racing primarily on flat

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the initial letters follow the word for flat

parts.note: even means flat or level, as in an even surface

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of each of the three words is used

parts.note: the three words whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A racehorse's trainers urge it on at a flat race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like flat racing in the surface, but it is EVEN; 'primarily' takes TER from 'trainers encourage racing', placed 'on' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, the equestrian contest of dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Essentially potty release price for component of Windows

indicators.note: the essence, or central letter, of the word

parts.note: middle letter of POTTY
a ransom is the price paid for a captive's release

explanation.surface: A mad demand to pay for part of Microsoft's operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital W makes it look like the software; a transom is a crossbar in a real window.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal bar across a window or above a door.

clue.text: Piece about island inhabited by unknown poet

parts.note: a chess or draughts piece is a man
on = about, as in a talk on a subject
standard abbreviation
x, y and z are the algebra unknowns

explanation.surface: An article about an island where an obscure poet lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown poet' reads as one phrase, but 'unknown' only gives the algebra letter, which inhabits the string built from piece, about and island.
explanation.definitionFit: Alessandro Manzoni was an Italian poet and novelist, author of I promessi sposi.

clue.text: Adult regularly wearing pig skin

indicators.note: wearing means having on like clothing, so the pig word goes round the picked letters

parts.note: a swine is a pig

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of adult is used

parts.note: the word adult, whose alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A grown-up is dressed in pigskin from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin' looks like the pigskin of the surface, but it is the definition, meaning cheat. 'regularly' takes DL from Adult, and SWINE is 'wearing' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To skin someone is slang for fleecing or cheating them, the same as to swindle.

clue.text: Way to classify alien

parts.note: ST = street
to range things is to arrange or class them

explanation.surface: A method for categorising extraterrestrials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' seems to be a noun needing classification; it is the adjective, meaning foreign or unfamiliar.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something alien is foreign and unfamiliar, and so strange to you.

clue.text: Smell ultimate in fear that's terrifying

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of fear
'eek!' is what you say at something terrifying

explanation.surface: A smell so bad it frightens people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's terrifying' is the reaction itself: the cry EEK.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as noun or verb: to give off a strong, usually foul, odour.

clue.text: Barren crop in mostly fluid ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the pooled letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of crop in, taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means most of it, so the last letter of fluid is dropped

parts.note: the word fluid, whose last letter goes

explanation.surface: A crop that fails in soggy, waterlogged soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil in the surface, but it is the anagram signal: FLUI (fluid 'mostly') joins 'crop in' and the letters are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprolific means not producing much offspring or fruit, so a barren field or animal is unprolific.

clue.text: Makes more stable companies

definitions.meaning: to firm (up) is to make firmer

explanation.surface: Companies strengthen their position.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence, subject after verb; it is really two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Firms is both a verb (makes firm) and a plural noun (businesses).

clue.text: Sound spanned by Port Hudson

indicators.note: the answer is bridged across the two words

parts.note: porT HUDson

explanation.surface: A strait or bridge crossing between two places named Port and Hudson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a stretch of water to match the port and river; it is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a thud is one particular sound, the dull noise of something heavy landing.

clue.text: Human attention beginning to be engaged by old character

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: to be engaged by is to be taken on and held

parts.note: thorn (þ) is an Old English letter for 'th'; it takes in B
first letter of be

explanation.surface: An ancient figure catches a person's attention as it begins to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' means an old letter, not a person: thorn. EAR + TH(B)ORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthborn means born on earth, and so human or mortal.

clue.text: Trunk's more or less on time

parts.note: standard abbreviation
'or so' = approximately, as in 'ten or so'

explanation.surface: A travel trunk that arrives roughly on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage or an elephant, but it is the body's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Your trunk is the main part of your body, the torso.

clue.text: Stressful period, arguably, if credit is doubled

indicators.note: doubled means made twice as many, so IS appears two times

parts.note: IF is in the middle of lIFe, so it is 'mid-life', arguably
CR = credit, in accounts
IS twice

explanation.surface: Doubling your credit could be a stressful time.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful step: IF sits in the middle of LIFE, so 'if' can be called MID-LIFE, and 'arguably' admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A midlife crisis is the anxious period some people go through in middle age.
